subject: Hosted API: data retention, snapshots, and deletion attestation
messages:
From: Amelia Rhodes <amelia.rhodes@cypra.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Li <mli@cypra.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - retention, backups, and legal hold questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Cypra's privacy team asked me to capture a few clarifying questions so we can close our security review:

1) What is the default retention window for request/response payloads sent to the hosted API (both raw request bodies and derived artifacts such as embeddings)?
2) How long are request logs/audit logs retained and are they stored separate from payloads?
3) We need to understand snapshot and backup retention (frequency, retention period, any long-term archival).
4) If we put an account under legal hold, what is the process to prevent deletion from backups/snapshots and how is that documented?
5) For erasure requests, can you provide an attestation that deleted data is removed from live systems and backups within stated windows?

Appreciate concise answers; our deadline for the security questionnaire is EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Rhodes
Security Program Manager | Cypra Analytics
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Rhodes <amelia.rhodes@cypra.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API - retention, backups, and legal hold questions

Amelia — thanks for the clear list. Below are direct answers and next steps; I attached a concise retention matrix (redwood_hosted_retention_matrix_v3.xlsx) for your legal/ops teams.

1) Payload retention (default):
- Request/response payloads (full-text): 90 days by default for hosted API customers.
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: 90 days by default; customers can request shorter windows at onboarding.

2) Logs and audit trails:
- Structured request logs (request metadata, timestamps, routing): retained 30 days by default.
- Security/audit logs (authentication events, console actions): retained 365 days for compliance traces.
- Logs are stored in a separate telemetry store (read-only indexes) and are not used to restore user payloads.

3) Snapshots / backups:
- Live-serving snapshots (KV caches, model state checkpoints): ephemeral; snapshots used for fault recovery are retained up to 7 days.
- Daily operational backups (for disaster recovery) are kept for 14 days in primary region; backups older than 14 days are automatically purged.
- No long-term archival of customer payloads is performed unless explicitly agreed in a contract (add-on).

4) Legal hold / preservation:
- We support account-level legal holds. Once requested, we flag the tenant in the control plane to prevent scheduled purges and to quarantine backups/snapshots relevant to the tenant for the hold duration.
- Legal holds are logged, have an owner and a ticket, and require an internal approval step (security & legal).

5) Erasure and attestation:
- Live deletion: when a deletion request is initiated, customer payloads are removed from the primary store within 72 hours (often sooner); any cached prefixes are invalidated immediately.
- Backups/snapshots: purged on the next backup cycle where applicable and within the 14-day backup window. For accounts with contractual shorter/longer windows we operate to the contract.
- We can provide a deletion attestation for completed erasure workflows as a signed PDF (we've attached a templated attestation in prior engagements).

Notes & caveats:
- These retention defaults apply to Redwood Hosted API (multi-tenant). Dedicated and Private deployments have configurable retention profiles.
- For EU data residency requests, we can isolate primary storage to EU-backed regions; retention and deletion mechanics remain the same but will operate inside the region.

Next steps: I attached the retention matrix and can follow up with a short attestation PDF once we confirm the exact retention windows you need. Kimberly and Ben are looped for legal/contract questions.

Regards,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood_hosted_retention_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Cypra Legal <legal@cypra.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API - retention, backups, and legal hold questions

Hannah,

Thanks — the matrix helps. A few follow-ups from Legal:
- We need explicit language about destruction of backups: does Redwood guarantee overwriting or cryptographic destruction of backup media where applicable once retention windows expire?
- Can Redwood commit to providing a signed deletion certificate for individual erasure requests that includes timestamps and the storage subsystems affected?
- If Cypra requests EU-only residency plus a 30-day payload TTL, confirm the timeline for backups/snapshots purge for that tenant.

Please advise and, if available, provide a redlined clause we can include in our procurement addendum.

Regards,
Lara Quinn
Senior Counsel | Cypra Analytics
legal@cypra.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lara Quinn <legal@cypra.com>, Amelia Rhodes <amelia.rhodes@cypra.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API - retention, backups, and legal hold questions

Lara — appreciate the precise asks. Short answers and formal commitments below; I included a deletion attestation PDF for your template and we'll follow contractual language for the addendum.

- Backup destruction: Redwood does not maintain long-term archival of customer payloads for hosted customers beyond the configured backup window. When backups/snapshots expire they are removed from object storage and accompanying indexes are deleted. Where underlying cloud provider supports it, we trigger object lifecycle deletes which make objects subject to provider immutable deletion policies. For customers requiring stronger guarantees we offer a contractual clause that includes periodic overwrite certification and retention-proof procedures (usually part of Dedicated/Private offerings).

- Deletion certificate: we can provide a signed attestation containing: tenant identifier, deletion request id, list of affected storage classes, timestamps (requested, processed, confirmed purge time), and an operator signature. See attached: redwood_deletion_attestation_cypra_20270623.pdf (templated; we will populate once a real erasure run completes).

- EU residency + 30-day TTL: Confirmed. For an EU-isolated tenant with a 30-day payload TTL we will:
  * Expire payloads from primary stores within 72 hours of a deletion call or at TTL boundary.
  * Remove payloads from the 14-day operational backups on the next daily backup rotation — effectively ensuring no retained backup beyond 44 days from initial write if no erasure requested earlier.
  * If you require backups to be pruned sooner we can propose a 7-day backup window for an additional compliance addendum.

I've cc'd Kimberly (contracts) and Ben (security product) to prepare language for an addendum and next steps.

Next steps:
- Kimberly will propose contract language for the deletion/backup clause by Friday EOD.
- Ben can schedule a brief tech walkthrough if Cypra wants to see purge traces and audit logs.
- I attached a populated attestation template you can use once we execute a live erasure.

Thanks — we can escalate to an exec approval if you need SLA exceptions.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_deletion_attestation_cypra_20270623.pdf (PDF, attestation template)
